ca_bubbs_creek_wall.blurb: A remote big wall in the High Sierra backcountry of Kings Canyon National Park, rising straight out of the Bubbs Creek drainage at roughly 7,400 feet. Getting here means a long day on foot up the canyon trail, so plan this as a committing multi-day objective rather than a quick outing. Ten climbs are recorded, mostly alpine-style trad lines of 15 to 19 pitches plus a couple of aid lines. The standard is steep and sustained: six of the ten sit in the 5.12 range, with only a few easier lines (roughly 5.2, 5.7, 5.10 and 5.11). Expect dikes, flakes, corners and roofs, and very few other parties.

ca_biddles_tower.blurb: A single sandstone tower boulder tucked off the main trail in the Castle Rock and Sanborn area of the South Bay, about 2,800 feet up in the hills above Santa Cruz. Problems line several of its faces, and there are ten of them, all bouldering. Most fall around V5 and V6, with a pair of easy V1s, one V3 and a single V7, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. Expect overhanging and arete-style problems with slopers and mantles. Landings can be awkward, with trees close to several problems, so bring a couple of pads and a spotter.

ca_north_luffenholtz_beach.blurb: A small, scenic rocky cove on the Humboldt coast just north of Houda Point, between McKinleyville and Trinidad. Ten climbs are recorded: eight sport routes, one trad line and a single easy boulder problem. Grades run from about 5.7 up to 5.11, with the bulk of them between 5.9 and 5.10, which makes it friendly for climbers building up to harder leads. The rock is decent rather than outstanding, a notch below nearby Houda Point and Moonstone. Because it depends far less on the tide than Houda does, it is a handy place to pass time waiting for the water to drop.
ca_north_luffenholtz_beach.parking_note: Use the Luffenholtz parking area, reached by driving about 0.8 miles north along Scenic Drive after leaving US-101 at the Westhaven exit.

ca_fisherman_s_boulders.blurb: A scatter of boulders south and east of Fisherman's Buttress, on the south shore of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains at around 7,100 feet. Ten problems are recorded, all bouldering, running from V1 to V4 and clustering at V3 (six of the ten), so it suits climbers working in the moderate range. The blocks are spread out across a steep, rocky hillside and reaching them involves a fair amount of scrambling over other boulders, so expect more walking than at a tidy roadside venue. Parking near the buttress is tight, especially on weekends.

ca_concrete_jungle.blurb: One of the enclosures in the abandoned Old LA Zoo in Griffith Park, now used for bouldering among the picnic grounds. The ten problems here run from very easy up to V7: roughly half are V1 or easier, then a scattering of V2 to V5 and one hard V7 test piece. It is the third enclosure in from the lot, with a medium-sized concrete slab in the middle and plenty of overgrown trees and plants, especially along the right wall. Short and urban, it works well for a quick session or for beginners rather than a destination day out.
ca_concrete_jungle.approach: A very short walk of under 500 feet from the Old LA Zoo picnic area lot; the boulders are in the third enclosure from the lot.

ca_1_roadside_distraction.blurb: A short cliff band on Raker Peak in Lassen Volcanic National Park, set closer to the road than the main Raker cliffs. The formations are shorter than they look but more overhanging than they appear, because of the slope at their base. Ten climbs are recorded, seven sport and three trad or top-rope, and the difficulty is high: only two sit around 5.10, while most are 5.12 and 5.13 with a single 5.14. It holds some of the hardest sport climbing in the park, with steep, pocketed and gritty rock, so it is a destination for strong sport climbers rather than beginners.
